extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: practicing scientists, naturalists, museum curators, geologists, seismologists, cartographers, and scientifically literate public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical standards for conducting, reporting, and popularizing scientific work across disciplines (distinguishing observation from theory, data presentation, map-making, seismology reports, museum displays, technical descriptions, pedagogy, and industrial practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of proof (nothing taken on faith)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is the first principle of science ... that nothing should be taken on faith, that we should prove all things, and take no step forward until we have made quite sure of our ground."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators (active researchers) must base claims on proof and careful verification rather than on untested assertions; distinguish investigators from popularisers who may rely on faith or opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism / hasty conclusions in popular science
rubrics_metrics.description: Many popular writers 'contradict in their practice the principles which men of science insist upon ... and encourage the habit of hasty conclusion instead of the spirit of scientific caution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those communicating science to the public should not prioritise sensational assertions over plain statements of fact; they must take the trouble to explain basic facts ('the alphabet of nature') and avoid confusing personal opinion with established truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish clearly between facts and hypotheses/theories
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is necessary to distinguish clearly between hypothesis or theory and scientific observation. Let facts be accumulated in as great a measure as possible, and theories too, in reasonable number, but let us be quite clear as to what are facts and what are theories...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accumulate extensive facts and limit the number of competing theories; always state explicitly which statements are observed facts and which are explanatory hypotheses, and indicate their relative value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat theories as working, not dogmatic, explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No true philosopher regards a hypothesis or theory as a Procrustean bed upon which all new knowledge must be placed, but only as a working or suggestive explanation of observed facts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use theories provisionally; be prepared to revise or discard theories when new observations conflict with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomic/reclassification standards: require demonstrable homologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxonomic changes should be supported by demonstration that organs and structures are paralleled and homologous (example: argument that Chaetognatha are primitive molluscs based on paralleled organs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions of long-standing classification require weighty anatomical or other evidence showing true homologies rather than superficial similarities; divergences must be assessed relative to known differences between established groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of seismological reports: clarity of conclusions vs tabulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Japanese seismogram publications provided 'a wealth of elaboration and tabulation which tends to obscure the conclusions drawn'; some conclusions run counter to generally held views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seismological (and similar data-heavy) reports should present data and tabulation in a way that leads clearly to interpretable conclusions; avoid excessive or poorly-structured tabulation that hides the argument or makes conclusions appear inconsistent with the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seismogram reproduction quality
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The value of the series of reproductions of forty-one seismograms ... would have been increased had the reproductions of Milne seismograms been less coarse in texture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality reproductions of instrumental records; poor reproduction texture can reduce the utility of the record to students and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical descriptions: report performance particulars (e.g., transmission distances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of a new wireless telephony microphone omitted 'particulars of distances over which transmission has been accomplished.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing inventions or technical devices, include concrete performance metrics (range, distances, conditions of operation) so claims can be assessed and reproduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartographic standards: appropriate scale and accuracy indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Prof. Hammer favours scale 1:25,000 'for ordinary publication' and 'lays great stress on the need for such maps bearing some indication of the degree of accuracy of the contour lines shown, as well as of the actual determinations of height upon which the contours depend.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose map scales suitable to the purpose (e.g., 1:25,000 for geological/economic purposes) and always indicate degree of accuracy of contours and the underlying height determinations used to draw them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological chart practice: up-to-date, regionally specific notes with explanatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly meteorological charts are 'replete ... with information of value to seamen' and include notes on ice, fog, charts for regions and explanatory text; differences arise from differing data sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the latest possible data, regional breakdowns, explanatory notes, and ancillary charts; note and explain inevitable differences when combining data from different sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum exhibition practice: accompany exhibits with explanatory guides
rubrics_metrics.description: A Linnean mementoes collection in the Natural History Museum is 'arranged ... and a small pamphlet, prepared by Dr. A. B. Rendle, explaining the different exhibits has been issued.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public displays and collections should be accompanied by clear explanatory material (pamphlets, guides) that explain items to visitors and contextualise exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication accessibility: prefer affordable or journal publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment that certain memoirs 'cannot be issued at a lower price, or, preferably, published in some recognised journal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly results should be published in accessible venues (affordable formats or recognised journals) to ensure wide dissemination and critical review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use oral traditions cautiously as historical evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: On the dating of the Zimbabwe temple: 'oral traditions ... are of little value' alone; they 'do not command perfect confidence, and they do not furnish conclusive evidence in disproof of the archaeological facts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat oral histories as supplementary evidence; corroborate them with archaeological, documentary, or other empirical evidence before using them to overturn material findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational textbook design: align with syllabuses and pedagogical reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Barnard and Child's geometry series 'provide students in any part of the Empire with courses of study which cover satisfactorily the revised syllabuses of examining bodies, and follow the reformed methods of geometrical teaching brought about by ... reports.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should be subdivided to meet differing educational standards, align with revised syllabuses, and adopt contemporary reformed teaching methods appropriate to student levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mining practice improvements: adoption of modern shafts, transport and drilling
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocated improvements include more vertical shafts, wider spacing of levels, more cross-cutting, better underground roads and tramproads, adoption of wire-rope and skips, compressed-air boring machines, and high explosives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern mining should prioritise good shafts, efficient underground and surface transport, mechanised drilling using compressed air, and adoption of contemporary ore-processing machinery to improve safety and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peat-industry production process (peat-moss litter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peat for peat-moss litter is dug in large sods, air-dried, disintegrated by rotating saws ('wolf'), sifted free from mould, and compressed into bales by vertical presses; mould and fines may be collected separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial production of peat litter should follow steps that ensure removal of mould, controlled disintegration, sieving, and compression into stable bales for storage and export; plant layout should move material efficiently from ground-floor 'wolf' to upper-floor baler with elevators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic indexing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Halbmonatliches Literaturverzeichnis 'fulfils its function of bringing the titles of papers published ... promptly before its readers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliographic services should promptly and comprehensively list new publications across relevant subfields, facilitating awareness among researchers.
